Subject: Recap & next steps — marketplace telemetry / subprocessor questions

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can make progress on the procurement checklist: 

Summary from our call:
- FinOps will evaluate Redwood for the cost observability feature via our Marketplace connector. Primary concerns: PII in logs, retention windows, audit logging, and third-party telemetry forwarding (Observix).
- You need a clear subprocessor roster, SOC 2 evidence, and an option to restrict telemetry that crosses into partner flows.

Action items I committed to: 
1) Share a short telemetry questionnaire (attached) so you can mark which fields are considered PII for your use case.
2) Provide our current subprocessor roster and DPA draft for review.
3) Confirm default retention and the controls we have to limit telemetry forwarded to marketplace partners.

Questions for you: 
- Can you confirm which identifiers you classify as PII (email, user id, IP, billing identifiers)? That will help us produce a tailored answer.
- Do you require data residency (EU/US) for marketplace-derived logs, or is tenant-level scoping sufficient?

Next steps: 
- If you can complete the attached questionnaire by EOD Wed (15 Sep), Marcus and I will produce a targeted statement of controls for the marketplace flow and return the DPA + subprocessor roster for legal review.
- If acceptable, Marissa will follow up with proposed contract language for subprocessor approvals and an action plan for restricted telemetry.

Attachments: telemetry-questionnaire.docx

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Best,

Vanessa — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from procurement/security side before we complete the questionnaire: 

What we treat as PII: email addresses, user IDs tied to identifiable customers, billing account ids. IP addresses are considered sensitive but we can sometimes accept hashed forms.

Retention requirements:
- Audit logs related to billing/usage must be retained for 365 days.
- For Marketplace telemetry we prefer a 90-day default retention for raw traces unless otherwise redacted.

Subprocessors & marketplace flows: 
- Observix (kristen@observix.com) is our preferred vendor for enrichment on the Marketplace side. We need confirmation that Observix will only receive metadata (no raw prompts / customer content) unless we explicitly approve.

Compliance evidence: we need a copy of Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II and confirmation you can provide support for a KMS/HSM integration (BYOK) for our dedicated accounts.

Timing: procurement would like to start contract negotiations the week of 20 Sep. Please indicate if Redwood can provide the roster & SOC2 by then.

Thanks,
Sam Hollis
Security & Procurement, FinOps Inc.

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — marketplace telemetry / subprocessor questions

Hi Sam — quick technical answers that map to your bullets (quoting only the Qs in-line):

> "Which identifiers you classify as PII?"
- We consider email, username, and billing identifiers PII by default. IP addresses are treated as semi-sensitive; by default we persist only hashed IPs in telemetry for 30 days. If you require hashing or truncation we can configure the connector to redact at ingest.

> "Retention requirements: 365 days / 90 days for marketplace telemetry"
- Hosted API default telemetry retention: 30 days for request bodies/prompt text, 90 days for structured event metadata. We can offer a contract-configurable retention policy for marketplace-derived telemetry: options are 30/90/365 days, subject to plan and whether you use Dedicated or Private deployment.

> "Observix — can you restrict to metadata only?"
- Observix is currently a marketplace integration partner. For Marketplace connectors we have an allowlist capability: Observix can be limited to receive only event metadata (timestamp, connector id, anonymized resource id) — we explicitly block prompt text and raw customer content unless a customer opt-in is approved. We can record the opt-in as a security-approved action in the Console.

> "SOC 2 Type II & KMS/BYOK"
- SOC 2 Type II (latest cycle) is available; I'll attach the cover letter and point you to the evidence portal. BYOK/KMS: Redwood supports KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. For hosted SaaS accounts we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (via AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) on request.

Artifacts attached: DPA_Redwood_Draft_Sept2027.pdf, subprocessor_roster_202709.pdf
Link to roster: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/roster-202709

If you can confirm the retention buckets you need and whether Observix must be fully excluded from receiving anything beyond metadata, I will draft a short statement of controls and a recommended configuration for your Marketplace connectors.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam / Vanessa — following Marcus's technical responses, a few legal points to keep momentum: 

- We can include a subprocessor approval clause in the DPA that requires Redwood to notify FinOps of any new Marketplace processors and gives you a 30-day objection window. - We'll add contract language for configurable retention windows (30/90/365) and a migration/certification path if you need Dedicated or Private deployment to meet residency guarantees.
- SOC 2 evidence: we will provide the SOC 2 cover letter and an access token to the evidence portal with reasonable redactions.

3) Week of 20 Sep: Commercial/Procurement kick-off to review redlines and PO timing.
